ranking.rationale: Best evidence-to-risk tradeoff: request-context features are the only screened family with positive lift (+0.002213), have full coverage, low leakage risk, low runtime risk, and require a clean single-family ablation.
Directly aligns training with within-user ranking and has low leakage risk. It is reasonably scoped, but expected gains are speculative and pair construction adds medium runtime risk.
Strong alignment with nDCG@5 and a clean loss-only ablation, but listwise implementation and impression-group handling create more feasibility and runtime uncertainty than BPR.

Tests a clear limitation of the additive seed by adding compact user-item affinity interactions. It is bounded and leakage-safe, though interaction overfitting and medium runtime risk weaken confidence.

A relatively contained training change with plausible GAUC benefit and low leakage risk. Evidence is indirect, and medium sampling complexity plus possible user-distribution distortion reduce expected value.

Combines the only positive feature family with interaction capacity, but changes architecture and features simultaneously, increasing attribution and validation-overfitting risk despite promising projected lift.

Potentially high upside from evolving user intent, but it has medium leakage risk, high runtime cost, substantial preprocessing scope, and weak direct evidence for the proposed sequential representation.
Hard negatives could improve top-five ordering, but this duplicates the BPR direction, depends on an unvalidated pairwise setup, and carries high runtime and sampler-noise risk.
Low-risk and temporally plausible, but expected gains are small and uncertain. Chronological batching changes optimization dynamics without direct evidence that it improves ranking.
Adds substantial nonlinear capacity without new evidence that ID-only interactions need it. High runtime and overfitting risk make it inferior to the simpler FM alternative.
Cheap and isolated, but optimizer choice has no supporting evidence and the expected gain is near zero with a plausible negative outcome.
Useful only as a diagnostic because it removes personalization and explicitly forecasts material GAUC and nDCG@5 degradation. It is not a good scarce experiment for maximizing performance.
